account: Today I have ordinary office duties, a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, afternoon council letters and tea with the neighbour. At eighteen I am to attend a thirty-minute public meeting in the great hall, with the secretary escorting me. The innkeeper requested it; the builder and freight operator form his committee. He says it concerns refreshments, deliveries and hall lighting for community gatherings, with residents welcome and no preparation needed. The neighbour intends to attend. What seems unusual is the scale of the bread order: the secretary reports the committee ordered 120 loaves, baked yesterday, but payment is unconfirmed. She has authorized none, and neither have I. I do not yet know who specifically placed the order, who promised payment, or precisely what gathering needs that much bread. I asked her to establish those facts with the committee before tonight. I also saw a lantern installed in the hall yesterday, consistent with their stated lighting arrangements, though that alone proves nothing further. My present impression is that practical preparations for a sizable gathering are already underway before the committee has explained the full plan to me. It could be straightforward civic hospitality, but the purpose and financing need clarification; I have no evidence of wrongdoing. I bought the secretary a writable book and left it in the appointments chest. She was absent when I returned, and I have heard no report on her inquiries. I have kept morning office hours and should shortly head to the mill.
